one_liner: Rust DWARF symbolication library plus addr2line-style CLI; first-party chart shows it beating binutils, elfutils and llvm-addr2line.
what_it_does: Maps code addresses to file, line, function name and the inline call stack using DWARF debug info. The library API is Loader::new(path) then find_location / find_frames / find_symbol, or a lower-level Context built from gimli::Dwarf when you manage the bytes yourself. A CLI (cargo feature 'bin') accepts a subset of GNU addr2line flags (-e, -f, -i, -a, -p, -s, -C, -j, --sup, --all, plus --llvm output style). It is also the symbolizer inside Rust's standard-library backtraces (rustc-dep-of-std feature) and the backtrace, wasmtime and blazesym crates.
how_it_is_fast: Lazy, cached parsing: a Context first builds a sorted table of unit address ranges (DW_AT_ranges, .debug_aranges, low/high pc) and binary-searches it per probe; a unit's line program, function DIEs and inlined-function tree are parsed only on first hit and memoised in OnceCell, so later lookups in the same unit are cheap. Loader memory-maps the file and borrows sections zero-copy (only compressed sections are decompressed into an arena). Abbreviation tables shared by many small units are cached (PR #318), which the maintainer reported roughly doubled speed on the PostgreSQL input, where gimli had been 2.12x slower than llvm-addr2line before the fix.
when_to_use: Long-lived processes that symbolize many addresses against the same binary (profilers, crash reporters, tracing tools): the parse cost is paid once per unit and amortised.
Batch symbolization of hundreds to thousands of addresses from large C/C++/Rust debug files (hundreds of MB), where the chart shows 2.6-16x over binutils addr2line.
Rust projects that need in-process symbolization without shelling out to binutils or llvm-symbolizer, including no_std + alloc targets (the Context API) and wasm (feature 'wasm').
Split DWARF (DWO/DWP), Mach-O dSYM bundles next to the executable, and DWARF supplementary files (--sup) on any platform the object crate parses.
when_not_to_use: Memory-constrained hosts: the README says it 'optimizes for speed over memory by caching parsed information', the benchmark measures time only, and issue #212 (2021, an older version) measured 2.6 GB RSS on a 470 MB libxul.debug against 1.3 GB for binutils.
One-off lookups of a handful of addresses: every CLI invocation reloads DWARF, and on the 38 MB postgres input it is only about 1.2x ahead of llvm-addr2line.

Scripts that rely on GNU addr2line's full option set or debug-file discovery: the CLI has no -b target, no demangling-style selection, and the Loader does not follow .gnu_debuglink or .gnu_debugaltlink (a TODO in src/loader.rs), so you must point -e at the .debug file and pass --sup yourself.
C or C++ codebases that want a C API: it is a Rust crate with no C bindings in this repo.
Binaries without DWARF (stripped, or PDB-only Windows builds): it falls back to the symbol table for function names only.

integration.form: crate (library) plus optional CLI binary via the 'bin' feature
integration.dependencies: gimli 0.34 (read); optional object 0.40, memmap2, typed-arena (loader feature), rustc-demangle, cpp_demangle, smallvec, fallible-iterator, clap (bin)
integration.platforms: any: no_std + alloc for Context; std and mmap for Loader; object files are parsed by the object crate (ELF, Mach-O with dSYM lookup, wasm behind the 'wasm' feature)
integration.thread_safety: Context is Send (asserted by a unit test) but not Sync, because lazy caches use core::cell::OnceCell; use one Context per thread or guard it with a lock.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: the CLI accepts the common GNU addr2line flags and stdin address streams, but lacks -b, demangle-style selection and debuglink discovery, and output equivalence with binutils is not tested by the benchmark

gotchas: Harness scope: the chart times whole CLI runs of '-af' only (no -i inlines, no -C demangling) and never compares outputs across tools; the address sample is drawn from gimli addr2line's own --all listing, and hyperfine --min-runs=1 means eu-addr2line and binutils are timed only once or twice per input (PR #315's sample output shows elfutils as a single run).

The chart is a one-off from 2024-08-06 (PR #325, around 0.24.x, Matplotlib metadata) and has never been regenerated for 0.25-0.27; tool versions come from an unpinned openSUSE Tumbleweed image whose Dockerfile names clang18 and postgresql16 debuginfo packages, so the image may not build as written today. No CPU, no RSS.

The speedups depend on fixes merged during the benchmarking work: PR #315's first sample had gimli at 391 ms vs llvm-addr2line 398 ms on clangd-18 (1.02x), and PR #318 notes gimli was 2.12x slower than llvm-addr2line on postgres before the abbreviation cache.
Maintainer stance on panics: issue #363 (0.25.1, unwrap on None in function.rs:205) was closed 'not planned' without a reproducer; malformed DWARF is otherwise returned as gimli::Error.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No symbolizer siblings are catalogued; the nearest entries (iced, Zydis, bddisasm, Intel XED) decode instruction bytes, not debug info. Pick addr2line when you need address-to-source-line and inline-frame resolution, typically alongside one of those disassemblers.
verified_claims_summary: Hyperfine mean wall time of 'addr2line -af -e <file>' over fixed-seed random address samples on four openSUSE Tumbleweed debuginfo files, chart read approximately: libxul.so 0.10 s vs binutils 1.15 s (about 11x), llvm-addr2line 0.48 s, eu-addr2line 3.25 s; clangd-18 0.18 s vs 2.92 s (about 16x); mold 0.14 s vs 1.19 s; postgres 0.067 s vs 0.176 s (about 2.6x) and llvm 0.079 s (about 1.2x). Rust stable from rustup in Docker, baseline tool versions and CPU not stated, chart dated 2024-08-06.
status_note: Actively maintained in the gimli-rs organisation (0.27.1, 2026-08-01; about 541M crates.io downloads, 77 reverse dependencies including backtrace and wasmtime) and dual Apache-2.0/MIT, so it is safe to depend on; the published speed chart is two years and three minor versions old.
